diagnosis: The gate failed because C7 (linked to PF3) failed in rollouts 0 and 3, and C1 (also linked to PF3) failed in rollout 3, leaving only 2 of 4 rollouts passing. In every failing case, PF3 was properly revealed by A4 and cited in justification_fact_ids, so this is not a disclosure or telepathy problem. In rollout 0, C7 failed because the model encoded the security commitment as type "security_remediation" with the word "applied" in the detail, whereas C7 appears to require "deploy/deployment" language — an ENCODING MISMATCH. In rollout 3, the model set rollout_approved=true (interpreting the security patch as a conditional prerequisite rather than a blocker), which caused both C1 (expecting approval withheld) and C7 (requiring the correct security decision plus a deployment commitment) to fail — also ENCODING MISMATCH, since the model's natural encoding of "approved with prerequisites" does not match the checks' expectation of rollout_approved=false.

fix_instructions: C7 (rollout 0, ENCODING MISMATCH): Broaden C7's commitment-matching logic to accept synonyms for deployment — e.g., "applied," "remediated," "patched" — in addition to "deployed/deployment." The model used type "security_remediation" with detail "Security patch must be applied…" which conveys the same commitment as the passing rollouts' "deployed" wording. Alternatively, add guidance in shared_context or the settlement schema instructing that security-patch commitments should use "deploy/deployment" terminology. C1 (rollout 3, ENCODING MISMATCH): Clarify C1's check description or add explicit guidance in shared_context that rollout_approved must be set to false whenever a blocking security finding exists, even if security_patch_before_rollout is true. The model in rollout 3 treated the patch as a precondition and still set rollout_approved=true, which two other rollouts correctly avoided. C7 (rollout 3, same root cause as C1): Because C7 requires both the correct security decision and a deployment commitment, the rollout_approved=true encoding error cascades into C7. Fixing the C1 encoding guidance will also resolve C7 in this case, since the commitment detail already contains "deploy and verify."
